Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall establish, capture, record, approve, and maintain software requirements, including for COTS/GOTS/MOTS/OSS/reused components, as part of the technical specification.
Our Interpretation: Governs whether the project has a requirements-management practice at all. An SRS could contain flawless requirements and still fail this if they were never approved or maintained.
Questions: Does 'approve' imply a baseline we could see evidence of in the SRS? Starhawk is marked 'Draft for Review' - our inference is not-yet-approved.

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall perform software requirements analysis based on flowed-down and derived requirements from top-level systems engineering requirements, safety and reliability analyses, and hardware specifications and design.
Our Interpretation: Concerns the derivation activity, not wording. Absence shows only indirectly: Starhawk section 10 lists mission needs but no allocation.
Questions: DISAGREEMENT: can we infer non-compliance from a missing traceability matrix, or is absence of evidence not evidence of absence?

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall include software-related safety constraints, controls, mitigations, and assumptions between the hardware, operator, and software in the software requirements documentation.
Our Interpretation: Performing the safety analysis is PROCESS, but 'include ... in the software requirements documentation' is checkable at SET/SRS level. Starhawk has REQ-014/015 (weapons inhibits) but no stated hazard analysis and no operator-vs-software allocation.
Questions: Likely the only 4.1 clause an automated reviewer could partially evaluate. Worth testing in a later sprint.

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall track and manage changes to the software requirements.
Our Interpretation: Pure change control. Nothing in the text of an SRS reveals whether it is satisfied.
Questions: Would a revision-history table count as evidence? We think not sufficient alone.

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall identify, initiate corrective actions, and track until closure inconsistencies among requirements, project plans, and software products.
Our Interpretation: 'Inconsistencies among requirements' is SET/SRS-detectable (Starhawk uses 'important', 'critical', 'safe' inconsistently and undefined). Inconsistency against plans and products is PROCESS.
Questions: Does detecting an inconsistency satisfy the clause, or is the corrective-action tracking also required? We read it as both, so an AI can flag but never demonstrate compliance.

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall perform requirements validation to ensure the software will perform as intended in the customer environment.
Our Interpretation: Validation involves stakeholders and an operational environment; it is not a property of text.
Questions: Define validation vs. verification separately in the taxonomy so we do not conflate them.

Guidance / Concept: Project manager shall perform, record, and maintain bi-directional traceability between software elements, applicability varying by software class (A-F).
Our Interpretation: Included because Starhawk section 10 admits no traceability matrix exists. NOTE: outside our assigned 4.1 scope - it sits in 3.12, project-wide process requirements. That placement is itself evidence traceability is process-level.
Questions: Should out-of-scope clauses appear here? Included, flagged, because the SRS raises the issue directly.

Guidance / Concept: Each requirement should be specific, testable, and traceable.
Our Interpretation: The handbook's general three-part criterion, stated for all CSCI requirements. Specificity and testability are judgeable from one sentence; traceability is not fully.
Questions: Stated twice on the page (Minimum Recommended Content and Guidance). This is the core rubric - the six-item list below is narrower in scope.

Guidance / Concept: Specific: clear and unambiguous, e.g. avoid subjective terms like 'efficient' or 'user-friendly'.
Our Interpretation: The most automatable criterion. Catches Starhawk REQ-016 'extremely accurate', REQ-021 'quickly', REQ-037 'without noticeable delay', REQ-050 'state-of-the-art'. Note the handbook names 'efficient' explicitly, and REQ-004 uses it verbatim ('safe and efficient route').
Questions: SCOPE NOTE: this six-item list is stated for FUNCTIONAL requirements specifically, not all requirements. Applying it to performance or security requirements is our extension, not the handbook's.

Guidance / Concept: Specific and verifiable/testable: each requirement should be clear enough to be tested with defined success criteria.
Our Interpretation: Catches REQ-040 ('shall never crash', an unprovable universal negative) and every unquantified qualifier.
Questions: DISAGREEMENT: how do we treat requirements testable in principle but missing information the SRS lacks (REQ-047, log capacity)? Defect, or missing context?

Guidance / Concept: Behavioral: define system behavior or operations under specific conditions.
Our Interpretation: Requires both a trigger condition and a defined response. Catches REQ-010, where the condition (engine failure) is given but the response ('appropriate corrective action') is not.
Questions: Is a requirement with a response but no stated condition equally defective? Not addressed.

Guidance / Concept: Complete: cover all expected inputs, outputs, and scenarios.
Our Interpretation: Cannot be judged from one requirement. Starhawk has no requirement covering Autopilot failure mid-route.
Questions: Hardest criterion to automate: detecting an absence requires knowing what should have been there. We should say so rather than promise it.

Guidance / Concept: Traceable: linked to user needs, business goals, or use cases.
Our Interpretation: Spans all three levels: whether a requirement carries a parent tag is INDIVIDUAL; whether every mission need is covered is SET; whether the matrix is maintained is PROCESS.
Questions: Best single example of one concept splitting across levels. Cite in ai_review_brainstorm.md.

Guidance / Concept: User-focused: describe how the system will respond to user inputs.
Our Interpretation: The weakest and most subjective of the six. Arguably style guidance rather than a testable criterion.
Questions: Include in the taxonomy at all? Risk of low-value findings. Leaning exclude.

Guidance / Concept: Use clear and consistent language; use 'shall' to indicate mandatory behavior.
Our Interpretation: Detectable per sentence.
Questions: INFERENCE: the handbook says use 'shall' for mandatory behavior but does NOT forbid 'shall' outside numbered requirements. Our Starhawk section 2.1 finding is an engineering inference, not a cited rule.

Guidance / Concept: Follow a structured format: include requirement ID, description, rationale, and acceptance criteria. Number each requirement for easy reference.
Our Interpretation: Starhawk has IDs and descriptions but NO rationale and NO acceptance criteria on any of the 54 requirements. Per-requirement this is INDIVIDUAL-checkable; as a documentwide omission it is SET/SRS.
Questions: Strong finding: this is a uniform gap across all 54, not scattered defects.

Guidance / Concept: Include exception and error handling: describe behavior under off-nominal situations including overflow, communication facilities, error handling and recovery, and relevant operational modes (nominal, critical, contingency).
Our Interpretation: Starhawk defines five operational modes but most requirements never state which mode they apply to. REQ-002 is a rare exception (names Manual Flight, Autopilot, Combat).
Questions: Is 'does not state its operating mode' a defect per requirement, or one set-level observation? Leaning set-level to avoid 50 near-identical findings.

Guidance / Concept: Prioritize requirements: identify which functions are critical vs. optional.
Our Interpretation: Starhawk has no priority or criticality field anywhere, though REQ-030 refers to 'critical faults' as though criticality were defined.
Questions: Related to the undefined-terms finding in initial_srs_observations.md section 8.

Guidance / Concept: Specify how the software requirements will be verified and validated, using the qualification methods: Demonstration, Testing, Analysis, Inspection.
Our Interpretation: Starhawk has NO Qualification Provisions section. Nothing in the document states how any requirement will be verified. This is a structural gap no individual requirement would reveal.
Questions: SWEHB is guidance, not binding like the NPR. Call this a 'recommendation not followed' rather than a defect, and word findings accordingly.

Guidance / Concept: Provide rationale, context, and justification for requirements; consider co-locating supporting rationale with each requirement.
Our Interpretation: Starhawk provides no rationale for any requirement. Section 10's mission needs are the closest thing, but they are not linked to individual requirements.
Questions: Would adding rationale have prevented the undefined thresholds? Plausible but unprovable - flag as hypothesis.

Guidance / Concept: An SRS should cover functional, non-functional, interface, and user requirements, including Safety, Security and Privacy, Fault Management, Fault Tolerance, Partitioning, and Computer Hardware Resource Utilization.
Our Interpretation: Useful as a completeness checklist. Starhawk covers functional, some performance and security, but has nothing on resource utilization (memory/CPU/storage), partitioning, or fault tolerance beyond REQ-040 to 043.
Questions: This is the most concrete completeness test available to us - a checklist of expected categories rather than open-ended 'what is missing?'.

Guidance / Concept: The SRS is revised as the project progresses; baselining for milestone reviews is covered by Topic 7.08, and requirements volatility is tracked per SWE-200.
Our Interpretation: Confirms that document maturity and change control sit outside the text itself.
Questions: Cross-references SWE-053 in our NPR rows above - consistent.
